reading.title: Two Languages, One Mind
reading.intro_zh: 这篇短文不复述法国搭车故事，而是介绍一个真实的语言科学话题：会两种语言的人，大脑里其实两种语言一直同时活跃。内容改编自《科学美国人》(Scientific American) 一篇关于双语大脑如何切换语言的报道。

source.title: How Brains Seamlessly Switch between Languages

passage: When two strangers fall silent because each assumes the other cannot understand a shared language, the awkward pause hides a remarkable fact about the human mind. According to research reported by Scientific American, the brain of a bilingual person never truly shuts one language off. Both languages remain active and accessible at the same time, even when the speaker is talking to someone who knows only one of them. Because of this constant parallel activation, a multilingual brain must continuously suppress the words it does not need, quietly resolving the competition between two vocabularies that are always ready to surface.

This hidden effort overturns a common assumption. Many people imagine that mixing languages, or switching rapidly from one to another, signals confusion or a deficiency. Neuroscientists argue the opposite. Using magnetoencephalography, which measures the tiny magnetic fields produced by neural activity, researchers tracked the brains of English-Korean bilinguals across hundreds of trials. They discovered that the same region, the left anterior temporal lobe, combines concepts into meaning regardless of which language supplies the words, and it does so without slowing down. Switching between languages is therefore neurologically natural rather than a flaw.

Strikingly, the studies suggest that holding to a single language can demand more cognitive control than alternating freely between two. Suppressing the unused language is genuinely taxing, so a bilingual speaker who must accommodate a monolingual listener may work harder than two bilinguals chatting comfortably. The silent travellers in our story, then, were not limited by their brains. Their minds were fully equipped for either language; only their mistaken assumption kept the conversation locked away.

questions.question: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Bilingual people should avoid mixing two languages in one sentence.
Learning a second language permanently damages the first one.
A bilingual brain keeps both languages active and switching between them is natural, not a flaw.
Most strangers stay silent because they genuinely share no common language.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文核心是：双语者大脑里两种语言一直同时活跃，语言之间的切换在神经层面是自然的，而不是缺陷。

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens to a bilingual person's two languages while they speak?
options: Both languages stay active at the same time, even when talking to a monolingual listener.
The unused language is completely switched off until it is needed.
Only the language learned first remains available in the brain.
The two languages take turns and are never active together.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中说 Both languages remain active and accessible at the same time，即使对方只懂其中一种语言。

questions.question: How did researchers study the bilingual brain in this passage?
options: By asking participants to fill in a written grammar test.
By comparing how fast people typed in two languages.
By recording how often bilinguals forgot common words.
By using magnetoencephalography to measure neural activity across many trials.
questions.explanation_zh: 研究者使用 magnetoencephalography（脑磁图）测量神经活动产生的磁场，并对英韩双语者做了数百次试验。

questions.question: What can we infer about the two silent travellers mentioned at the end?
options: Their brains were unable to handle a second language.
Their silence came from a wrong assumption, not from any limit of the mind.
They had each forgotten how to speak their shared language.
Speaking two languages had made them too tired to talk.
questions.explanation_zh: 最后一段指出他们的大脑完全有能力使用任一语言，沉默只是源于错误的假设（only their mistaken assumption kept the conversation locked away）。

questions.question: In the passage, the word "suppress" most nearly means to
options: hold back or keep from surfacing.
translate quickly into another language.
speak loudly and with confidence.
forget completely and permanently.
questions.explanation_zh: suppress 指大脑把暂时不需要的语言“压住、不让它冒出来”，即 hold back or keep from surfacing，与 forget（彻底遗忘）不同。

writing.intro_zh: 今天抓 Lesson 14 的五个核心句式，并把例句提升到 B2+ 难度：用 After I had... 写过去故事里更早发生的动作，用 asked me for... 写求助，用 As soon as... 写紧接着发生的动作，用 Apart from a few words...at all 写能力极其有限，最后用 Neither of us... 写尴尬或迟疑的沉默。

patterns.title: After I had ..., I ...
patterns.source: After I had left a small village, I drove on to the next town.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 After I had... 表示一个动作在过去故事里更早发生，然后再写下一步动作。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写你先完成了某个准备或决定，之后才在一个较抽象或正式的情境（如研究、旅行、面试、谈判）里采取下一步行动。
patterns.sample: After I had carefully weighed every option, I finally decided to delay the project until the budget was approved.
patterns.tip_zh: had 后面接过去分词，后半句用一般过去时写下一步动作。

patterns.title: asked me for ...
patterns.source: He asked me for a lift.
patterns.focus_zh: asked me for... 用来写别人向我请求某种帮助、信息或东西。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一个陌生人、同事或访客在某个具体场景里向你请求帮助、信息、建议或指引，并补充一点背景。
patterns.sample: A confused tourist at the crowded station asked me for directions to the museum, although she barely spoke the local language.
patterns.tip_zh: for 后面接名词或名词短语，比如 help, advice, directions, a seat。

patterns.title: As soon as ..., ...
patterns.source: As soon as he had got into the car, I said good morning to him in French.
patterns.focus_zh: As soon as... 强调前一个动作刚发生，后一个动作马上跟着发生。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某件事刚一发生，你或别人立刻采取了一个有结果或有影响的行动，场景尽量正式或抽象。
patterns.sample: As soon as the negotiations had collapsed, the two delegations quietly withdrew their offers and prepared for a longer dispute.
patterns.tip_zh: 如果要强调过去故事里的先后顺序，可以在 as soon as 后面用 had done。

patterns.title: Apart from a few words, ... at all
patterns.source: Apart from a few words, I do not know any French at all.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个结构用来承认自己只知道很少一点，并用 at all 加强否定语气。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：承认在某个专业领域、语言或技能里你只掌握极少的内容，其余几乎一无所知，并点出这带来的影响。
patterns.sample: Apart from a few words of medical jargon, I do not understand the specialist's report at all, which makes me nervous.
patterns.tip_zh: Apart from a few words 放在句首，后面通常接 do not know...at all。

patterns.title: Neither of us ...
patterns.source: Neither of us spoke during the journey.
patterns.focus_zh: Neither of us... 强调两个人都没有做某件事，适合写沉默、犹豫或误会。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写两个人因为误会、紧张或不确定而都没有开口或行动，并暗示这种沉默造成的后果。
patterns.sample: Neither of us dared to break the tense silence, so a simple misunderstanding slowly hardened into a lasting resentment.
patterns.tip_zh: Neither of us 后面的动词通常用单数形式，比如 speaks/is/knows；写过去故事时用 spoke/was/knew。
